name: Incap Electronics US, Inc.
about:
Incap Electronics US, Inc. operates from a 6,500-square-meter facility in Coal Center, Pennsylvania. The site has over 26 years of electronics manufacturing experience and employs 124 people. It is the U.S. arm of Incap Corporation, a global EMS provider listed on Nasdaq Helsinki since 1997, and is led by Managing Director David Spehar.

The facility specializes in complex printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) using advanced surface-mount and through-hole technologies, supported by in-circuit testing, functional testing, validation, conformal coating, selective soldering, and precision assembly. Engineering services include design for manufacturability, test development, prototyping, new product introduction, hardware and software development, embedded systems, industrial IoT, and power electronics R&D. The company also provides mechatronics, cable and wire harness assembly, magnetic assembly, electronics protection, box build, control cabinets, clean room production, and automotive-grade EMS. Full product support covers global sourcing, fast-track programs, customized solutions, final configuration, fulfillment, and after-sales MRO.

Incap US serves customers in energy, power and charging; defence and aerospace; and e-mobility and automotive sectors. Typical applications include metering infrastructure, gas detection systems, industrial electronics and control systems, medical devices, and sensor-based technologies. The company emphasizes long-term partnerships, with many customer relationships exceeding 20 years.

Incap US differentiates itself through a local, customer-driven approach backed by a global manufacturing network. The team prioritizes fast decision-making, direct communication, and proactive problem-solving to keep production running smoothly. A focus on process control, robust testing, and product stability aims to deliver total cost of ownership and long-term reliability over short-term cost optimization.

about:
Ind. Co. Cable TV, operating as Indco.net, has been based in Batesville, Arkansas since its founding in 1976. The company has served the region for over four decades, though the input does not specify its ownership structure or founders.

The company provides cable television and internet services across north-central Arkansas. Its internet offerings include fiber-to-the-home connections, DOCSIS 3.0 cable broadband, and fixed wireless service, with speeds up to 1 Gbps. Service areas encompass Cave City, Pfeiffer, Newark, Magness, Gum Springs, Searcy, Beebe, McRae, Forrest City, Colt, Caldwell, Cushman, Judsonia, Plainview, Pleasant Plains, and Pangburn. The company also handles billing and network maintenance.

Indco.net serves both residential and business customers in its coverage area. The input does not detail specific industry verticals beyond general telecommunications and cable television services.

The company emphasizes a customer-focused, human-driven approach and a commitment to a free and open web, offering unlimited data with no caps on all packages. It positions its service as straightforward, with no complicated setup required.

Independent Beverage Company operates from Charlotte, North Carolina, where it was founded in 1991. The company is privately held, though ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

The company specializes in cold-fill beverage production, running PET bottle and can lines for soft drinks, sparkling water, and other non-alcoholic beverages. It serves as a contract packager and private-label bottler, handling various package sizes and flavors. Its facility near the intersection of Interstates 77 and 85 includes production, warehousing, and office space, though exact square footage and headcount are not published.

Independent Beverage works with national brands, retailer private-label programs, and contract-pack customers. Its client list includes well-known names such as Cheerwine, Canada Dry, Sun Drop, 7-Up, Sunkist, A&W, Country Time, Hawaiian Punch, and Sunny D. The company also markets its own CLEAR FROST™ line of sparkling waters.

The company emphasizes its SQF Food Safety certification as a core differentiator, underscoring a focus on quality and compliance in cold-fill beverage manufacturing.

name: Indiana Rubber & Plastic, LLC
old_description: We specialize in custom molded plastics and rubber. We offer turnkey service from idea to prototypes to volume production with custom molding and low-cost alternatives.
about:
Indiana Rubber & Plastic, LLC was founded in 1936 in Indianapolis, Indiana, and has operated continuously for three generations. The company began as a specialist in custom molded plastics and rubber and has expanded its capabilities while remaining focused on its core expertise.

The company provides turnkey service from prototyping through high-volume production. Its processes include rubber molding (compression, transfer, injection, and LSR/LIM), plastic injection molding, extrusion of both plastics and rubber, die cutting, lathe-cut rubber, machined plastics, and bonded rubber-to-metal components. Prototyping uses 3D printing, SLA, rapid molding, and silicone molds. Production volumes span prototype runs of 1–50 pieces, short runs of 1–5,000 pieces, medium runs of 5,000–25,000 pieces, and high-volume orders exceeding 25,000 pieces. The facility operates high-tonnage presses with large platens for oversized parts and maintains on-site tooling to match mold size to demand.

Indiana Rubber & Plastic serves customers requiring custom molded rubber and plastic components, including those needing food-grade and military-specification materials. Its product portfolio includes grommets, gaskets, seals, bumpers, diaphragms, bushings, extrusions, mounts, formed hoses, boots, and washers or spacers.

The company differentiates itself through competitive pricing driven by innovation, an in-house technical team of designers, CAD drafters, chemists, and laboratory resources, plus access to custom compounders. It emphasizes a "plastics and rubber" breadth—adding urethane, silicone, and thermoplastic elastomers—and a commitment to staying within its three generations of core knowledge. Transparent communication throughout the supply cycle and proprietary Amazing Tool$aver® low-cost tooling methods further define its approach.

name: Indusco Wire Rope & Fittings
old_description: We’re excited to share an important update about Indusco Wire Rope & Fittings. Since 2011, Indusco has proudly operated under the Mazzella Companies as a standalone business. Over the years, we’ve grown together—supporting our customers with a shared commitment to service, safety, and reliability.
about:
Indusco Wire Rope & Fittings, based in Baltimore, Maryland, has operated under the Mazzella Companies since its acquisition in 2011. Mazzella was founded in 1954 by James Mazzella in Cleveland, Ohio, and remains a privately held, family-owned business. The merger formalizes a long-standing relationship, with Indusco becoming part of Mazzella's Industrial Distribution/Reseller Division effective August 2025.

The company supplies a broad range of lifting and rigging products, including wire rope, slings and assemblies, rigging hardware, cordage, fall protection, and engineered lifting devices. It also fabricates overhead cranes, provides crane and hoist service and repair, and offers OSHA-mandated inspections and rigging training. Mazzella operates more than 40 locations across North America with over 1,300 employees, and the Baltimore facility at 2209 C Sulphur Spring Road serves as a regional hub.

Primary markets include mining, steel, oil and gas, construction, energy, shipbuilding, and vehicle and durable goods manufacturing. Customers range from industrial contractors to OEMs requiring lifting solutions and safety compliance services.

Mazzella emphasizes a no-excuses, customer-first mentality from shop floor to front office, aiming to deliver faster response times and streamlined operations through consolidated resources and a single national brand.

The company references clients such as M & S Equipment Services and Matrix Integrated, the latter noting that IAE responded after hours to restore production machinery. IAE highlights its 50‑plus years of experience, a fully stocked local warehouse, and knowledgeable staff as key differentiators. The company states that its focus on fast, reliable procurement helps customers minimize downtime and keep projects on schedule.

old_description: WELLER,Electronic Supply by Industrial Electronics in Milwaukee Wisconsin : Potter Brumfield, Radio Shack Stores...
about:
Industrial Electronics By Ross LLC operates from West Allis, Wisconsin, where it was founded in 1927 as a supplier of tubes and radio parts. The company is a woman-owned small business and functions as an employee-managed organization, with 99 percent of sales decisions made at the first level.

Today the firm acts as a franchised distributor for more than 116 electronic manufacturers, offering access to over one million items ranging from electron tubes to integrated circuits. Its product portfolio includes chemicals such as acrylic coatings, contact cleaners, and flux removers, as well as heat-dissipative products like cold plates and extrusions. The company also operates as a just-in-time (JIT) supplier for industrial customers.

The business serves the industrial marketplace, providing electronic parts and services to customers in sectors that require reliable component sourcing. Its franchised lines cover brands such as Potter & Brumfield, Weller, and Molex, supporting applications in industrial automation, automotive electronics, and general electronic assembly.

The company emphasizes its employee-managed structure as a differentiator, stating that frontline staff make nearly all sales decisions, which it says enables faster response times. Its JIT supply capability and broad franchised manufacturer base are presented as core reasons customers choose the firm.

name: Industrial Fabrics, Inc.
old_description: Since 1981, Industrial Fabrics has proudly served many diverse clients in the construction, industrial and residential industries along the Gulf Coast and around the world.
about:
Industrial Fabrics, Inc. (IFI) was founded in 1981 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. The company began as a pioneer in the geosynthetic industry, developing synthetic products to solve civil and geotechnical engineering problems. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

IFI manufactures and distributes a range of geosynthetic solutions including geogrids, geotextiles, geomembranes, and erosion control systems under brands such as RockGuard, GrassGuard, EnviroTubes, GreenSolutions, and BaseLok. A new $8 million production facility enables full-service manufacturing and custom fabrication. The company supports design assistance, material logistics, and on-site technical support, with over 5,000 projects completed across more than 20 states.

The firm serves engineers, contractors, and government agencies in sectors including commercial and industrial development, roadways, railways, energy, residential, marine and waterways, ports, airports, data centers, electrical, petrochemical, oil and gas, waste management, military, mining, and temporary housing.

IFI emphasizes engineered solutions backed by on-staff registered engineers, ISO-certified manufacturing, and continuing education seminars. Its mission focuses on strengthening infrastructure through innovation, integrity, and sustainability, with a reach extending from the Gulf Coast to global projects.

name: Industrial Finishes
old_description: Industrial Finishes is proud to be Featuring 3M products Since 1958
about:
Industrial Finishes, headquartered in Reno, Nevada, has been featuring 3M products since its founding in 1958. The Reno location originated from the acquisition of Barrett Paints and Re-Neva Paint, with the facility refreshed in 2012 to include a dedicated training center capable of hosting up to 50 people.

The company distributes paint finishes, industrial coatings, paint supplies, surface preparation materials, hand power tools, equipment, abrasives, safety products, and clips and fasteners. It also provides business support and educational training, including painter certification, color matching, paint line conversion, mixing system training, and shop process evaluation. Industrial Finishes operates four regional training centers and offers on-site and video-enabled instruction. The Reno team collectively holds over 100 years of experience, and the location serves a 150-mile radius as the primary paint supplier for Lake Tahoe and Reno.

Industrial Finishes serves the automotive, RV and specialty vehicle, military, industrial/panel, equipment sales, infrared curing, construction, and aerospace/defense sectors. Concrete customers include Drone America, one of the largest drone providers for the U.S. government, and local construction firms. The company's philosophy centers on "rolls, floats, or flies" applications, developing finishing systems for virtually any substrate.

The company emphasizes a "national presence, local support" model, stating that the sale is just the beginning of their duty and they strive to re-win business daily through timely delivery of quality products. Their guiding principles include openness, accountability, risk-taking within limits, a commitment to doing it right, learning from mistakes, integrity, collaboration, and courage in the face of difficulty.

name: Industrial Metal Enterprises, LLC
old_description: Let us provide you with your auger needs and screw flights using our Super Tyro AST machine utilizing Tru-Helix flight forming technology.
about:
Industrial Metal Enterprises, LLC was founded in 1993 in Blackfoot, Idaho, operating as a limited liability company serving Eastern Idaho. The business began as a metal fabrication shop and has grown into a full-service contractor for industrial, commercial, and residential clients.

The company runs a machine shop equipped with a Haas TM-2P CNC mill (40" x 16" x 16" travel, 10,000 RPM spindle) and a water jet cutter, alongside CNC plasma cutting capacity. Its signature capability is a Super Tyro AST machine with Tru-Helix flight forming technology, described as the only such machine in the western United States, used to produce custom augers and sectional screw flights. The shop fabricates structural steel, stainless steel, carbon steel, aluminum, and specialty metals into conveyors, decks, platforms, handrails, stairs, sheet metal flashings, and ornamental pieces. Welding, pipe fitting, boiler and steam fitting, and mobile welding services round out the offering. In-house design produces 3D drawings for customer approval before fabrication.

Primary markets include food processing, where sanitary design conveyors and equipment are a focus, as well as broader industrial, commercial, and residential construction across Eastern Idaho. Customers range from food plants needing auger flights and sanitary conveyors to contractors requiring structural platforms, stairs, and custom metalwork.

The firm emphasizes on-time delivery and installation, competitive pricing, and the ability to take complicated, unique designs from concept through completion. Its Tru-Helix system reduces reliance on operator expertise for consistent screw flights, and the Haas TM-2P adds high-speed machining for precision parts.
